html: Transition metals carried on particles turn hydrogen peroxide into the hydroxyl radical, the most reactive oxygen species. Ferrous iron does it in the Fenton reaction, cuprous copper in its copper analogue, and chromium as it is reduced from chromate, Cr(VI), towards Cr(III): chromate enters cells through sulfate transporters, glutathione reduces it to Cr(V), and the intermediate states react with hydrogen peroxide. Each metal is recycled to its reduced form, so a small amount of metal can make radicals for as long as peroxide is supplied.
